title: Menus and Shortcuts
summary: A main menu bar turns a pile of windows into an application - File, Edit, View, Tools. This lesson covers menu bars in the main viewport and in windows, menu items with checkmarks and shortcut text, the Begin/End rule for menus, and wiring the shortcuts so they actually work.
markdown:
## The main menu bar

```cpp-norun
if (ImGui::BeginMainMenuBar())                       // across the top of the screen
{
    if (ImGui::BeginMenu("File"))
    {
        if (ImGui::MenuItem("New level", "Ctrl+N")) newLevel();
        if (ImGui::MenuItem("Open...", "Ctrl+O"))   openDialog();
        if (ImGui::MenuItem("Save", "Ctrl+S", false, level.dirty)) save();   // disabled when nothing changed
        ImGui::Separator();
        if (ImGui::MenuItem("Quit", "Alt+F4")) running = false;
        ImGui::EndMenu();
    }
    if (ImGui::BeginMenu("View"))
    {
        ImGui::MenuItem("Stones", nullptr, &showStones);    // a checkmark bound to a bool
        ImGui::MenuItem("Log", nullptr, &showLog);
        ImGui::EndMenu();
    }
    ImGui::EndMainMenuBar();
}
```

This is the pair rule you met in lesson 1.04: `BeginMainMenuBar`/`EndMainMenuBar` and `BeginMenu`/`EndMenu` are only ended **if their Begin returned true**. A closed menu returns `false`, so its `EndMenu` is skipped.

`MenuItem` has two useful forms:

- `MenuItem(label, shortcut, selected, enabled)` returns `true` when clicked; `selected` draws a checkmark, `enabled = false` greys it out.
- `MenuItem(label, shortcut, bool* selected)` toggles the `bool` when clicked: the standard "show window" switch.

Menus can nest: a `BeginMenu` inside another opens a sub-menu.

## A menu bar inside a window

```cpp-norun
ImGui::Begin("Level editor", nullptr, ImGuiWindowFlags_MenuBar);
if (ImGui::BeginMenuBar())
{
    if (ImGui::BeginMenu("Edit")) { /* ... */ ImGui::EndMenu(); }
    ImGui::EndMenuBar();
}
// window contents
ImGui::End();
```

## Shortcut text is only text

The second argument of `MenuItem` ("Ctrl+S") is **only displayed**. Clicking the menu item works; pressing Ctrl+S does nothing unless you also check the keys. Do that once, outside the menu code, so the shortcut works even when the menu is closed:

```cpp-norun
if (ImGui::Shortcut(ImGuiMod_Ctrl | ImGuiKey_S, ImGuiInputFlags_RouteGlobal)) save();
```

A tidy approach is a table of **commands**: each has a name, a shortcut, an "is it available" check and an action. The menu draws from the table, the shortcut handler checks the table, and a command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P, like editors have) can list it too. The practice builds that table, including detecting two commands that claim the same shortcut.

## Keyboard navigation in menus

With `ImGuiConfigFlags_NavEnableKeyboard`, pressing **Alt** focuses the menu bar, arrow keys move through it, Enter activates and Escape closes, the way desktop applications behave.

## Common mistakes

> [!warning] Calling EndMenu when BeginMenu returned false
> ImGui asserts. EndMenu goes inside the if.

> [!warning] Expecting the shortcut text to work by itself
> It is a label. Check the keys with Shortcut or IsKeyPressed.

> [!warning] Two commands on the same shortcut
> Only one will ever run, depending on which is checked first. Detect clashes when you build the command table.

## Check yourself
```quiz
? Which menu functions follow the "End only if Begin returned true" rule?
- Only BeginMenu/EndMenu; the menu bars always need their End call
- None of them; menus always need their End call, like windows
+ BeginMainMenuBar/EndMainMenuBar, BeginMenuBar/EndMenuBar and BeginMenu/EndMenu
- Only BeginMainMenuBar/EndMainMenuBar
> All three menu pairs are ended only when their Begin returned true. `Begin`/`End` for windows is the exception that always calls `End`.

? How do you make a menu's shortcut actually work?
- Pass the shortcut text as MenuItem's second argument, and ImGui detects the keys
+ Check the key chord yourself, for example with `ImGui::Shortcut`, once per frame outside the menu code
- Check the keys inside the `BeginMenu` block, next to the MenuItem
- Enable `ImGuiConfigFlags_NavEnableKeyboard`
> The shortcut text is only a label. Checking the keys inside the menu block would only work while the menu is open.

? Why build menus from a command table?
- Because ImGui can only draw menus from an array of items
- Because a table makes the menu draw faster than separate calls
- So that each command can be given more than one shortcut key
+ One list drives the menu, shortcuts and palette, and catches shortcut clashes
> The table is your own design, not something ImGui needs; its value is that everything about a command, including when it is available, lives in one place.

? BeginMenu("File") returns false because the menu is closed. What do you do?
- Call EndMenu anyway, so the Begin/End calls stay balanced
+ Skip its items and do not call EndMenu
- Call BeginMenu again next frame with a different label
> Menus follow the "End only if Begin returned true" rule; calling EndMenu after a false Begin makes ImGui assert.

? What does the "Ctrl+S" argument of MenuItem do?
- It registers a global shortcut for that item
- It sends Ctrl+S to the window when the item is clicked
+ It is shown next to the item; it does not detect the keys
> It is display text only. Detect the shortcut separately.

? Which MenuItem form toggles a bool when clicked?
+ `MenuItem(label, shortcut, &flag)`
- `MenuItem(label, shortcut, flag, true)`
- `MenuItem(label, shortcut, false, flag)`
> The `bool*` form flips the bool for you, which is ideal for showing and hiding windows. The `bool` forms only draw a checkmark or enable the item.
```
ideas:
- Give your tool a main menu bar with File, Edit and View menus, and View items that show and hide its windows.
- Make Ctrl+S, Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y work both from the menu and from the keyboard.
